phases.objective: Add a fail-closed, no-secret, read-only Production privilege verification path for the dedicated Governance DB writer without duplicating Production DB credentials into GitHub Actions and without provisioning accounts, grants, secrets, deployment, or migration apply authority.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Repository privilege matrix evaluator, opt-in Hostinger runtime deployment-info readiness projection, and exact-head manual readiness workflow
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The exact Production runtime can prove the required direct table privilege matrix using Hostinger-local DB configuration while the GitHub workflow receives only bounded no-secret evidence, rejects runtime/ref drift, and never receives database credentials.
steps: Load the repository-defined Governance DB privilege matrix.
Accept normalized information_schema privilege rows without a database connection in synthetic regression coverage.
Prove the exact required direct table privileges are accepted.

Reject missing required privileges, schema-wide privileges, unexpected global privileges, unrelated table scopes, extra operations on allowed tables, column-level grants, and applicable MariaDB roles.
Reuse one live probe service for CLI and Hostinger runtime execution so the privilege contract cannot drift between paths.
Expose only an opt-in cached bounded readiness projection through deployment-info; do not expose usernames, database names, raw privilege rows, role names, or missing-grant details.
Require an exact Production branch SHA and explicit confirmation token before the GitHub workflow collects runtime evidence.
Require the running deployment SHA and branch to match the authorized exact Production state.
Re-read the protected Production ref after runtime evidence and fail closed on movement.
Do not supply DB_* or GOVERNANCE_DB_* values to the GitHub runner.
Do not create users, execute GRANT, mutate application rows, deploy, restart, or run migration SQL in this source slice.
assertions: The required privilege matrix is identical to the reviewed #6813 Production contract.
The synthetic evaluator fails closed when any required privilege is missing.
The synthetic evaluator fails closed on any schema-wide privilege or unexpected global privilege.
The synthetic evaluator fails closed on unrelated table/schema grants and extra privileges on allowed tables.
The synthetic evaluator fails closed on column-level privilege paths and applicable MariaDB roles.
The runtime probe composes with resolveGovernanceProductionPreflight() and therefore cannot treat main as Production authority or reuse runtime DB credentials as Governance credentials.
The public runtime projection omits raw privilege details and credential-bearing identity/target values.
The GitHub workflow contains no DB_* or GOVERNANCE_DB_* secret bindings and performs no database connection itself.
The workflow proves exact runtime SHA and branch before accepting the privilege verdict and re-reads Production afterward.
No Production SQL mutation, CREATE USER, GRANT, provider mutation, deployment, restart, or Migration 1050 readiness/apply is performed by CI for this PR.
